en.etichetta_trattato: From the treatise De motu locali · in Latin in 1638; here in the English of Crew and de Salvio
en.note:
Text. Galileo Galilei, Dialogues Concerning Two New Sciences, translated from the Italian and Latin into English by Henry Crew and Alfonso de Salvio, with an introduction by Antonio Favaro (New York, Macmillan, 1914; public domain), in the transcription of the Online Library of Liberty (Liberty Fund), which allows free use for educational, non-commercial purposes. Crew and de Salvio follow the National Edition (Favaro), essentially the Leiden edition of 1638. The translators' footnotes and the page numbers are omitted.

How the English is aligned. The page follows the paragraphs of the Italian edition, so that the language menu keeps your place. The 389 speeches of Salviati, Sagredo and Simplicio correspond one to one; the propositions of the treatise are matched by number. Between these anchors the English sentences are assigned to the Italian paragraphs by a script that compares the letters of the geometrical points and the numbers, which do not change with the language: where the two editions divide paragraphs differently, a sentence may fall in the neighbouring paragraph.

The Latin treatise. In 1638 the treatise De motu locali, read by Salviati in the Third and Fourth Days, is printed in Latin. The Italian edition used for the Italian page (UTET, 1980) gives only the statements; Crew and de Salvio translate the whole treatise, demonstrations included: here they are in the paragraph of the corresponding statement. The three lemmas before Proposition XXXVI of the Third Day, a corollary to Proposition XXXVII and the lemma before Proposition X of the Fourth Day, absent from the Italian edition, appear in bold within the text.

The Appendix on the centres of gravity of solids is not part of the Crew–de Salvio translation: the Italian text is given.

The demonstrations in the panels. The Latin is transcribed by the editors from the 1638 printing (copy digitised by Google Books, file “Galilei - Discorsi e dimostrazioni matematiche intorno a due nuove scienze - 1638.djvu” on Wikimedia Commons, public domain); the English is that of Crew and de Salvio. The facsimile in the uniform-motion panel is cut from the same printing (p. 152).

The figures of the text (96) come from the LaTeX source of the Italian edition; whether they reproduce the 1638 engravings or are redrawings is still to be checked.
